hypothesis: Moving SPCX Swing to observation-only in addition to the three commodity Swing routes already retired by inactive v32 will remove a historically unstable and live winner-concentrated route while preserving SPCX breakout pressure, SP500 Swing, both-side visibility, and every unrelated portfolio contract.
decision: Supersede inactive v32 with inactive v33. V33 changes only the SPCX Swing execution symbol from executable to observe-only relative to v32. Relative to active v25, SNDK, GOLD, BRENTOIL, and SPCX Swing are observe-only; their breakout-pressure controls remain executable, SP500 Swing remains executable, and all nine assets remain visible in both directions. Do not arm or transition v33 automatically. Live v25 remains authoritative with four protected open positions. A future v33 transition requires an exact-fingerprint transition contract, completed drain, verified flat and order-free boundary, immutable prechange backup, placement-free reconciliation, explicit live-risk authorization, and candidate-specific post-start acceptance.
falsifier: Invalidate v33 if its parsed v32-to-v33 diff changes anything beyond SPCX Swing execution authority, if SPCX observation or either side disappears, if SP500 Swing or any SPCX breakout authority changes, if evidence hashes drift, or if the candidate gains automatic transition or execution authority. Revise the economic recommendation if preregistered independent SPCX Swing evidence survives both sides, observed costs, validation, largest-winner removal, and shared-router interaction.
limitations: V33 is an inactive candidate and has not been reconciled, launched, or tested as a new live run.
The live SPCX evidence contains only three long trades; it cannot estimate a stable expectation or either-side behavior.
The 317-trade SPCX study tested a finite side and timing family on opened development and validation partitions; it does not reject untested causal mechanisms.
Removing one provider route can expose or displace later same-symbol opportunities; shared-router economics require prospective tracking.
BTC, HYPE, GOLD, and BRENTOIL remain open and protected, so no portfolio-wide flat transition boundary currently exists.
One mutable source-code reference in historical journal revision 2 reports hash drift after tracker generalization; all evidence bound by this revision is immutable and matching.
No live process, profile, route, order, stop, target, position, size, leverage, or protection changed.
